title: Backpacking, Storms and Climbing in the Uinta Mountains
summary:
Leaving Lander, we decided to hightail it out of Wyoming and head to the Uinta Mountains in Northern Utah. First, though, we made a pit stop in Rock Springs, WY, not because there is anything to do there, but because it had a Planet Fitness and Walmart. We made it to Mirror Lake Highway, a road that passes through the Unita mountains, just in time to find a dispersed site off the road, make dinner, watch Iron Chef and get to bed. We moved camp the next day, just a couple miles down the road to a more private site among the aspens. We spent most of the day relaxing, reading and packing our gear for the backpacking trip we were doing the next day.

On our morning drive to the trailhead we spotted multiple moose, chomping on grass in the big meadow near the start of the trail. The trail to our destination, Amethyst Lake, was about 6.5 miles long, meandering (sometimes extremely steeply) up the mountain through forest, grassy meadows, and across many little streams. Maya had the time of her life frolicking and rolling in the marshy meadows. We made it to the lake in the early afternoon, and although it was a little busy with fellow backpackers, we found a nice private spot to set up camp. We spent that afternoon reading and fishing, and caught our very first fish on our new fly fishing setup! The lake was set against some big rock walls, and we heard multiple big rock slides throughout the evening, which was pretty wild. We cooked up our backpacking meals, only to discover one was rancid, but we supplemented with trail mix and cuties. We got into bed just as the sun was setting and watched the rock wall turn orange while reading in the tent, away from the pesky mosquitoes.

The following day, we set out to try to summit Ostler Peak, the big mountain looming over us at camp. After maybe about a 6th of the way up, and after struggling on loose rock in the direct sun, I decided to call it quits on that endeavor and pivot our adventure to hike to a couple of lakes we could see from our vantage point. We had a nice little picnic lunch at Ostler Lake before heading back to camp for the afternoon. It was a very hot day, so we had a refreshing dip in the lake. We spent the afternoon reading and fishing some more, and Maya spent it huddled in the tent, escaping the flies. After catching a few more trout, we decided to keep one of the bigger ones (still quite small) to try to cook it up. Colin handled the cleaning of the fish (his first time), and we cooked it up with some butter and salt, it was quite delicious!

The next morning, after very little sleep (we have become quite accustomed to our big comfy van bed), we packed up and made the hot hike down to the car. We drove just a few miles down the same road to a nice little pullout shaded by trees where we unpacked and took a very refreshing shower out the back of the van. We spent the rest of that day relaxing and hiding from the sun.

Over the next few days, we bopped between different campgrounds in the Uintas, climbing and hiking. It is a beautiful area at about 10,000 ft with lots of little lakes and blooming wildflowers. The monsoons seem to have arrived in earnest in the last week or so, and we experienced a big storm one afternoon, where it hailed for almost two hours, created big thunderclaps and left the road to our dispersed site looking more like a stream. After that bit of excitement, we left the dispersed site in search of a campground with pavement. Our friends Tyson and Maddy met us that night on the way to their family reunion, and we had a fun morning of climbing the next day. After that, my brother Al met up with us for a couple of nights of camping a little farther down the road towards Salt Lake. We spent two nights all together hanging out, playing Splendor, going on a big day hike, and watching Sheep Detectives. The next morning we rolled through Salt Lake to see his place, shower, do a desperately needed load of laundry and stock up on goodies at Trader Joes.

-Helen
